## Appendix D Further Reading

### D.1 Canonical Papers by Topic

Each cluster below maps to one or more chapters in this book. Clusters 1-2 supportchapter 3andchap-
ter 13-chapter 14. Clusters 3-5 map tochapter 6-chapter 7andchapter 8-chapter 10. Clusters 6-9 support
chapter 15-chapter 19. Cluster 10 maps tochapter 20-chapter 22. Clusters 11-12 supportchapter 26-chapter 28
andchapter 23-chapter 25. Format: _Title_ - Authors (last names) - one-line description.

**1. Transformer Architecture & Attention**

**_Attention Is All You Need_** - Vaswani, Shazeer, Parmar, Uszkoreit, Jones, Gomez, Kaiser, Polosukhin - In-
troduces the Transformer: encoder-decoder architecture built entirely from multi-head self-attention and feed-
forward layers, replacing recurrence.

**_RoFormer: Enhanced Transformer with Rotary Position Embedding_** - Su, Lu, Pan, Murtadha, Wen, Liu

- Proposes Rotary Position Embedding (RoPE), encoding position by rotating query/key vectors so that dot-
product attention captures relative distance naturally.

**_Fast Transformer Decoding: One Write-Head Is All You Need_** - Shazeer - Introduces Multi-Query Atten-
tion (MQA), sharing a single key-value head across all query heads to reduce KV-cache memory and decoding
latency.

**_GQA: Training Generalized Multi-Query Transformer Models from Multi-Head Checkpoints_** - Ainslie, Lee-
Thorp, de Jong, Zemlyanskiy, Lebron, Sanghai - Proposes Grouped-Query Attention (GQA) as an interpolation
between MHA and MQA, providing near-MQA speed with quality close to full multi-head attention.

**_FlashAttention: Fast and Memory-Eﬀicient Exact Attention with IO-Awareness_** - Dao, Fu, Ermon, Rudra,
Re - Rewrites attention computation with tiling to avoid materialising the fullNNattention matrix, cutting
HBM traffic and achieving 2 - 4 speed-up.

**_FlashAttention-2: Faster Attention with Better Parallelism and Work Partitioning_** - Dao - Refines FlashAt-
tention with improved thread-block scheduling and reduced non-matmul FLOPs to nearly double throughput on
A100/H100 GPUs.

**_DeepSeek-V2: A Strong, Economical, and Eﬀicient Mixture-of-Experts Language Model_** - DeepSeek-AI

- Introduces Multi-Head Latent Attention (MLA), compressing KV projections into low-rank latent vectors to
reduce KV-cache by up to 93 .3%without quality loss.

**_Train Short, Test Long: Attention with Linear Biases Enables Input Length Extrapolation_** - Press, Smith,
Lewis - Presents ALiBi, adding a linear bias to attention logits based on token distance so models trained on
short sequences generalise to longer ones at inference.

**_GLU Variants Improve Transformer_** - Noam Shazeer - Studies Gated Linear Unit variants including SwiGLU
(swish-gated FFN) and shows they consistently outperform standard ReLU feed-forward layers.


```
D.1 Canonical Papers by Topic
```
**2. Scaling Laws**

**_Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models_** - Kaplan, McCandlish, Henighan, Brown, Chess, Child, Gray,
Radford, Wu, Amodei - Establishes empirical power-law relationships between model parameters, dataset size,
compute budget, and validation loss for autoregressive language models.

**_Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models_** - Hoffmann, Borgeaud, Mensch, Buchatskiy, Cai,
Millican, van den Driessche, Clark, Casas, Guy, Hendricks, Jones, Menick, Hernandez, Jakub, Hubert, Vinyals,
Osindero, Kavukcuoglu, Simonyan, Rae - The “Chinchilla” paper, showing that previous models were over-
parameterised and under-trained; optimal compute budget splits equally between model size and token count.

**_Scaling LLM Test-Time Compute Optimally_** - Snell, Lee, Xu, Kumar, Garg, Sharan, Abbeel, Levine, Ghosh

- Demonstrates that allocating more computation at _inference time_ (e.g. best-of-Nsampling, process-reward-
guided search) can match gains from scaling parameters.

**_Tensor Programs V: Tuning Large Neural Networks via Zero-Shot Hyperparameter Transfer_** - Yang, Hu,
Babuschkin, Sidor, Liu, Farhi, Ryder, Pachocki, Chen, Gao - Introduces Maximal Update Parameterisation (μP),
enabling hyperparameter tuning on small proxy models that transfer to large models without retuning.

**3. Mixture of Experts**

**_Outrageously Large Neural Networks: The Sparsely-Gated Mixture-of-Experts Layer_** - Shazeer, Mirho-
seini, Maziarz, Davis, Le, Hinton, Dean - Introduces the conditional-computation MoE layer with a learned
routing gate, scaling model capacity to 137B parameters without proportional compute cost.

**_Switch Transformers: Scaling to Trillion Parameter Models with Simple and Eﬀicient Sparsity_** - Fedus, Zoph,
Shazeer - Simplifies MoE routing to top-1 (single-expert) selection and demonstrates stable trillion-parameter
training with strong downstream performance.

**_Mixtral of Experts_** - Jiang, Sablayrolles, Roux, Mensch, Savary, Bamford, Chaplot, de las Casas, Hanna,
Bressand, Lengyel, Bour, Lample, Lavaud, Saulnier, Lachaux, Stock, Gall, Acharya, Gottesman, Ourry, Rastogi,
Roelofs, Sanseviero, de Vries, Launay - Presents Mixtral 87B (and 822B), a sparse MoE model using top-2
routing that matches or exceeds dense models many times its active parameter count.

**_DeepSeekMoE: Towards Ultimate Expert Specialisation in Mixture-of-Experts Language Models_** - Dai,
Deng, Zhao, Xu, Gao, Chen, Li, Zeng, Yu, Wu, Xie, Li, Huang, Luo, Liang, Chen, Liu, Dai - Proposes fine-
grained expert segmentation with shared plus routed experts, achieving higher specialisation and efficiency than
standard top-krouting.

**4. Distributed Training & Parallelism**

**_Megatron-LM: Training Multi-Billion Parameter Language Models Using Model Parallelism_** - Shoeybi,
Patwary, Puri, LeGresley, Casper, Catanzaro - Introduces intra-layer (tensor) model parallelism for Transform-
ers, enabling efficient multi-GPU training of models too large for a single device.

**_Eﬀicient Large-Scale Language Model Training on GPU Clusters Using Megatron-LM_** - Narayanan, Shoeybi,
Casper, LeGresley, Patwary, Korthikanti, Vainbrand, Kashinkunti, Bernauer, Houston, Tulloch, Shi, Singh,
Catanzaro - Combines tensor, pipeline, and data parallelism (“3D parallelism”) with interleaved pipeline schedul-
ing to train 1T-parameter models efficiently.


```
D.1 Canonical Papers by Topic
```
**_GPipe: Eﬀicient Training of Giant Neural Networks Using Pipeline Parallelism_** - Huang, Cheng, Bapna,
Firat, Chen, Chen, Lee, Gong, Shen, Wu, Le - Proposes pipeline parallelism with micro-batching and gradient
accumulation to train models across multiple accelerators in a synchronous fashion.

**_PipeDream: Generalized Pipeline Parallelism for DNN Training_** - Narayanan, Harlap, Phanishayee, Se-
shadri, Devanur, Ganger, Gibbons, Zaharia - Introduces asynchronous 1F1B (one-forward-one-backward) pipeline
scheduling to overlap communication and computation, reducing idle pipeline bubbles.

**_ZeRO: Memory Optimizations Toward Training Trillion Parameter Models_** - Rajbhandari, Rasley, Ruwase,
He - Proposes Zero Redundancy Optimizer (ZeRO), partitioning optimizer state, gradients, and parameters
across data-parallel ranks to remove memory redundancy without increasing communication volume signifi-
cantly.

**_PyTorch FSDP: Experiences on Scaling Fully Sharded Data Parallel_** - Zhao, Gu, Varma, Luo, Huang,
Xu, Wright, Shojanazeri, Ott, Sheng, Bhatt, Shen, Abid, Truong, Bhosale, Mihailescu, Patel - Describes Py-
Torch’s production FSDP implementation, detailing sharding strategies, mixed precision, and the API choices
made for usability at scale.

**5. GPU Kernels & Hardware**

**_FlashAttention: Fast and Memory-Eﬀicient Exact Attention with IO-Awareness_** - Dao, Fu, Ermon, Rudra,
Re - (See Cluster 1.) The foundational IO-aware kernel paper; listed again here as the exemplar of GPU-level
memory hierarchy optimisation for DL.

**_Triton: An Intermediate Language and Compiler for Tiled Neural Network Computations_** - Tillet, Kung,
Cox - Introduces the Triton DSL that lets researchers write high-performance GPU kernels in Python without
hand-coding CUDA, with tiling handled by the compiler.

**_NVIDIA H100 Tensor Core GPU Architecture_** - NVIDIA - Official architecture whitepaper covering the
Hopper SM, fourth-generation Tensor Cores, NVLink 4.0, and the new Transformer Engine with FP8 support.

**_CUTLASS: Fast Linear Algebra in CUDA C++_** - Kerr, Nicholls, Tanner, Naumov, Young, Coles, Mer-
cat, Noel, Haluza, Kerr (NVIDIA) - Describes CUTLASS, NVIDIA’s open-source template library for high-
performance GEMM and convolution operations that underlies cuBLAS and many DL frameworks.

**6. Inference Systems**

**_Orca: A Distributed Serving System for Transformer-Based Generative Models_** - Yu, Jeong, Kim, Kim,
Jeong, Cho, Shin - Proposes _iteration-level_ (continuous) batching so that finished sequences are immediately
evicted and new requests join the batch without waiting, greatly improving GPU utilisation.

**_Eﬀicient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention_** - Kwon, Li, Zhuang,
Sheng, Luo, Foster, Flammarion, Huang, Stoica, Zhang - Introduces PagedAttention, storing KV-cache in non-
contiguous memory pages analogous to OS virtual memory, eliminating fragmentation and enabling flexible
sharing for vLLM.

**_Accelerating Large Language Model Decoding with Speculative Sampling_** - Chen, Borgeaud, Irving, Lespiau,
Sifre, Jumper - Shows that a small draft model can proposektokens in parallel, which the large target model
verifies in a single forward pass, yielding lossless 2 - 3 decoding speed-up.

**_Fast Inference from Transformers via Speculative Decoding_** - Leviathan, Kalman, Matias - Independent


```
D.1 Canonical Papers by Topic
```
concurrent work establishing the same speculative-decoding framework with formal acceptance-rejection proofs
preserving the target distribution exactly.

**_Medusa: Simple LLM Inference Acceleration Framework with Multiple Decoding Heads_** - Cai, Li, Geng,
Peng, Lee, Chen, Dao - Adds multiple lightweight “Medusa heads” to a frozen LLM to predict several future
tokens simultaneously, enabling tree-based speculative decoding without a separate draft model.

**_Eﬀiciently Programming Large Language Models using SGLang_** - Zheng, Yin, Xie, Huang, Sun, Yu, Cao,
Kozyrakis, Stoica, Gonzalez, Barrett, Sheng - Presents SGLang, a structured generation language that fuses
RadixAttention (prefix-tree KV-cache reuse) with a runtime for complex, multi-call LLM programs.

**7. KV-Cache Reduction**

**_GQA: Training Generalized Multi-Query Transformer Models from Multi-Head Checkpoints_** - Ainslie, Lee-
Thorp, de Jong, Zemlyanskiy, Lebron, Sanghai - (See Cluster 1.) Reduces KV-cache by a factor equal to the
group size by sharing key/value heads across groups of query heads.

**_Eﬀicient Streaming Language Models with Attention Sinks_** - Xiao, Tian, Chen, Han, Lewis - Observes
that a small number of “attention sink” tokens attract disproportionate attention, enabling infinite-length gener-
ation by maintaining only sinks plus a sliding-window cache ( _StreamingLLM_ ).

**_H 2 O: Heavy-Hitter Oracle for Eﬀicient Generative Inference of Large Language Models_** - Zhang, Sheng,
Jiang, Chen, Li, Guo, Zhu, Zheng, Gonzalez, Stoica, Re - Identifies “heavy-hitter” tokens that accumulate the
most attention mass and proposes a greedy eviction policy that preserves them to maintain quality under aggres-
sive KV-cache budgets.

**_SnapKV: LLM Knows What You Are Looking for Before Generation_** - Li, Zhang, He, Guo, Qian, Zhang,
Ma, Shan, Yang, Yin - Clusters per-head attention patterns from a short observation window at prefill time to
select and compress the KV-cache before long generation begins.

**_DeepSeek-V2: A Strong, Economical, and Eﬀicient Mixture-of-Experts Language Model_** - DeepSeek-AI

- (See Cluster 1.) MLA compresses the joint KV projection into a single low-rank latent vector, reducing per-
token KV-cache size by 93 .3%relative to standard MHA.
**8. Beyond-Transformer Architectures**

**_Mamba: Linear-Time Sequence Modeling with Selective State Spaces_** - Gu, Dao - Introduces a selective
state-space model (SSM) with input-dependent gating that matches Transformer quality on language modelling
while scaling linearly in sequence length.

**_RWKV: Reinventing RNNs for the Transformer Era_** - Peng, Alcaide, Anthony, Albalak, Arcadinho, Bi-
derman, Cao, Cheng, Chung, Derczynski, et al. - Proposes RWKV, reformulating attention as a linear recurrence
that admits both parallel training (like Transformers) and constant-memory inference (like RNNs).

**_Jamba: A Hybrid Transformer-Mamba Language Model_** - Lieber, Lenz, Bata, Cohen, Osin, Dalmedigos,
Safahi, Meirom, Belinkov, Shalev-Shwartz, Shoham - Interleaves Transformer (attention) and Mamba (SSM)
layers with MoE feed-forwards, combining the long-context efficiency of SSMs with the in-context learning
strength of attention.


```
D.1 Canonical Papers by Topic
```
**9. Compression & Quantization**

**_GPTQ: Accurate Post-Training Quantization for Generative Pre-trained Transformers_** - Frantar, Ashkboos,
Hoefler, Alistarh - Uses second-order (Hessian) information via the Optimal Brain Quantisation framework to
quantise large LLMs to 3-4-bit weights with minimal perplexity degradation.

**_AWQ: Activation-Aware Weight Quantization for LLM Compression and Acceleration_** - Lin, Tang, Tang,
Yang, Dang, Han - Identifies salient weight channels by observing activation magnitudes and protects them from
quantisation error, enabling efficient 4-bit inference without retraining.

**_SmoothQuant: Accurate and Eﬀicient Post-Training Quantization for Large Language Models_** - Xiao, Lin,
Seznec, Wu, Demouth, Han - Migrates quantisation difficulty from activations to weights by per-channel scaling,
making both amenable to INT8 without accuracy loss.

**_LLM.int8(): 8-bit Matrix Multiplication for Transformers at Scale_** - Dettmers, Lewis, Belkada, Zettlemoyer

- Shows that emergent large-magnitude outlier features in activations cause INT8 degradation, and proposes
mixed-precision decomposition to quantise99.9% of weights to INT8 while keeping outliers in FP16.

**_DistilBERT, a distilled version of BERT: smaller, faster, cheaper and lighter_** - Sanh, Debut, Chaumond,
Wolf - Demonstrates knowledge distillation for Transformers, training a 40%-smaller student BERT that retains
97% of teacher performance on GLUE via soft-label and hidden-state matching.

**_LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models_** - Hu, Shen, Wallis, Allen-Zhu, Li, Wang, Wang,
Chen - (See Cluster 11.) Also a compression technique: decomposing weight updates into low-rank products
reduces trainable parameters by 10 , 000 compared with full fine-tuning.

**10. Data Pipelines**

**_CCNet: Extracting High Quality Monolingual Datasets from Web Crawl Data_** - Wenzek, Lachaux, Con-
neau, Chaudhary, Guzman, Joulin, Grave - Presents the CCNet pipeline: language identification, deduplication,
and quality filtering of Common Crawl at scale; foundational for many subsequent pre-training corpora.

**_The Pile: An 800GB Dataset of Diverse Text for Language Modeling_** - Gao, Biderman, Black, Golding,
Hoppe, Foster, Phang, He, Thite, Nabeshima, Presser, Leahy - Introduces a curated, diverse 800 GB dataset
from 22 high-quality sources, providing an open training corpus and evaluation of data diversity effects.

**_The RefinedWeb Dataset for Falcon LLMs: Outperforming Curated Corpora with Web Data Only_** - Penedo,
Malartic, Hesslow, Cojocaru, Cappelli, Alobeidli, Pannier, Almazrouei, Launay - Shows that massively dedu-
plicated and filtered Common Crawl data ( _RefinedWeb_ ) can outperform manually curated mixtures, challenging
assumptions about the necessity of diverse high-quality sources.

**_Dolma: An Open Corpus of Three Trillion Tokens for Language Model Pretraining Research_** - Soldaini,
Kinney, Bhagia, Schwenk, Atkinson, Magnusson, Authur, Chandu, Dror, Fang, et al. - Releases a fully open 3T-
token corpus from AI2 with detailed provenance and filtering documentation, enabling reproducible pre-training
research.

**_Deduplicating Training Data Makes Language Models Better_** - Lee, Ippolito, Carlini, Chang, Uszkoreit,
Carlini, Litwin - Demonstrates that near-duplicate removal (MinHash LSH) from pre-training corpora reduces
memorisation and improves downstream task generalisation.


```
D.1 Canonical Papers by Topic

**11. Alignment & Post-Training**

**_Training Language Models to Follow Instructions with Human Feedback_** - Ouyang, Wu, Jiang, Almeida,
Wainwright, Mishkin, Zhang, Agarwal, Slama, Ray, Schulman, Hilton, Kelton, Miller, Simens, Askell, Welin-
der, Christiano, Leike, Lowe - The InstructGPT paper: SFT on human demonstrations followed by PPO against
a reward model trained on human preference comparisons, establishing the canonical RLHF pipeline.

**_Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback_** - Bai, Jones, Ndousse, Askell, Chen, DasSarma, Drain,
Fort, Ganguli, Henighan, Joseph, Kadavath, Kernion, Conerly, El-Showk, Elhage, Hernandez, Hume, Kaplan,
Lovitt, Nanda, Olsson, Amodei, Brown, Clark, McCandlish, Olah, Mann, Amodei, Clark - Trains a harmless as-
sistant using a written “constitution” of principles: supervised learning from self-critique and RLAIF, removing
dependence on human preference labels for harmlessness.

**_Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model_** - Rafailov, Sharma,
Mitchell, Ermon, Manning, Finn - Derives a closed-form training objective from the RLHF reward-maximisation
problem, enabling preference-based alignment without an explicit reward model or PPO.

**_DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning_** - DeepSeek-AI

- Trains reasoning models with Group Relative Policy Optimisation (GRPO) and verifiable outcome rewards,
achieving OpenAI-o1-level performance while open-sourcing weights and methodology.

**_LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models_** - Hu, Shen, Wallis, Allen-Zhu, Li, Wang, Wang,
Chen - Freezes pre-trained weights and injects trainable rank-decomposition matrices into attention projections,
reducing fine-tuning memory and compute by orders of magnitude.

**_QLoRA: Eﬀicient Finetuning of Quantized LLMs_** - Dettmers, Pagnoni, Holtzman, Zettlemoyer - Com-
bines 4-bit NormalFloat quantisation (NF4) of the frozen base model with LoRA adapters and paged optimisers,
enabling full-parameter-equivalent fine-tuning on a single consumer GPU.

**12. Evaluation**

**_Measuring Massive Multitask Language Understanding_** - Hendrycks, Burns, Basart, Zou, Mazeika, Song,
Steinhardt - Introduces MMLU: 57 subjects spanning STEM, humanities, and social science, providing a broad
measure of world knowledge and academic reasoning.

**_Beyond the Imitation Game: Quantifying and Extrapolating the Capabilities of Language Models_** - Sri-
vastava, Rastogi, Rao, Shoeb, Abid, Fisch, Brown, Santoro, Gupta, Garriga-Alonso, et al. - Presents BIG-Bench:
204 tasks collaboratively designed to probe model capabilities beyond standard benchmarks, with analysis of
scaling behaviour.

**_HellaSwag: Can a Machine Really Finish Your Sentence?_** - Zellers, Holtzman, Bisk, Farhadi, Choi - Con-
structs adversarially filtered commonsense NLI completions that are trivial for humans but hard for models,
exposing the gap between surface statistics and genuine understanding.

**_Evaluating Large Language Models Trained on Code_** - Chen, Tworek, Jun, Yuan, de Oliveira Pinto, Ka-
plan, Edwards, Burda, Joseph, Brockman, Ray, Puri, Krueger, Petrov, Khlaaf, Sastry, Mishkin, Chan, Gray,
Ryder, Pavlov, Power, Kaiser, Bavarian, Winter, Tillet, Such, Cummings, Plappert, Chantzis, Barnes, Herbert-
Voss, Guss, Nichol, Paino, Tezak, Tang, Babuschkin, Balaji, Jain, Saunders, Hesse, Carr, Leike, Achiam, Misra,
Morikawa, Radford, Knight, Brundage, Murati, Mayer, Welinder, McGrew, Amodei, McCandlish, Sutskever,
Zaremba - Introduces HumanEval: 164 hand-written Python programming problems with unit tests for pass@k

**_Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena_** - Zheng, Chiang, Sheng, Zhuang, Wu, Zhuang,
Lin, Li, Li, Xing, Zhang, Gonzalez, Stoica - Introduces MT-Bench (multi-turn instruction-following) and Chat-
bot Arena (human pairwise voting), establishing LLM-as-a-Judge as a scalable evaluation methodology aligned
with human preference.

**_Holistic Evaluation of Language Models_** - Liang, Bommasani, Lee, Tsipras, Soylu, Yasunaga, Zhang, Faber,
Wu, Bharadwaj, et al. - Presents HELM: a holistic evaluation framework that measures accuracy, calibration,
robustness, fairness, bias, and efficiency across dozens of scenarios and model families.

**Recommended Reading Order**

1. **Architecture foundations first.** Start with _Attention Is All You Need_ (Cluster 1), then _FlashAttention_ and
    _GQA_ - these three papers underpinchapter 3and are the most frequently cited in interviews.
2. **Scale and compute.** Read Kaplan et al. then Chinchilla back-to-back (chapter 13-chapter 14). MuP (μP) is
    optional unless you are interviewing for a training infrastructure role.
3. **Systems stack.** Orca!PagedAttention!speculative decoding (Cluster 6) mirrorchapter 15andchap-
    ter 18; add ZeRO and Megatron-LM (Cluster 4) for training roles.
4. **Alignment capstone.** InstructGPT, DPO, and DeepSeek-R1 together span the full post-training landscape
    covered inchapter 26-chapter 28. Read them in that order.

### D.2 Blogs, Talks, and Engineering Reports

The entries below cover flagship model technical reports and practitioner blogs that put flesh on the theory
developed across Parts I-XI. Model reports (GPT-4, Llama 3, Gemini, DeepSeek) are the best place to see
how the concepts inchapter 3-chapter 14manifest at production scale. Infrastructure and alignment blogs
complementchapter 11,chapter 15,chapter 19, andchapter 26-chapter 28. Format: _Title_ - Publisher/Company

- one-line description.
**13. Engineering Blogs and Technical Reports**

**Flagship Model Technical Reports**

**_GPT-4 Technical Report_** - OpenAI - Describes GPT-4 capabilities, evaluations (including bar-exam, MMLU,
vision), and safety mitigations; notable for its detailed model-card approach while withholding architectural
specifics.

**_The Llama 3 Herd of Models_** - Meta AI - Covers the full Llama 3 family (8B-405B), detailing pre-training
data curation, supervised fine-tuning, RLHF, and safety alignment with publicly released weights.

**_Llama 2: Open Foundation and Fine-Tuned Chat Models_** - Touvron, Martin, Stone, Albert, Almahairi,
Babaei, Bashlykov, Batra, Bhargava, Bhosale, et al. (Meta AI) - Introduces Llama 2 and Llama 2-Chat, docu-
menting the SFT-then-RLHF training recipe, ghost attention, and iterative red-teaming for safety.

**_Gemini: A Family of Highly Capable Multimodal Models_** - Google DeepMind - Presents the Gemini 1.0
family (Ultra, Pro, Nano), covering multimodal architecture, training at scale, and benchmark results across text,
code, image, audio, and video.


```
D.2 Blogs, Talks, and Engineering Reports

**_Gemini 1.5: Unlocking Multimodal Understanding Across Millions of Tokens of Context_** - Google Deep-
Mind - Details Gemini 1.5 Pro’s million-token context window via a sparse MoE architecture and efficient
attention, enabling long-document and long-video understanding.

**_PaLM 2 Technical Report_** - Google - Documents the PaLM 2 model family with improved compute-optimal
training (Chinchilla scaling), multilingual capability, and reasoning improvements over PaLM.

**_DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning_** - DeepSeek-AI

- Open technical report detailing GRPO-based reinforcement learning on verifiable reasoning tasks, cold-start
strategies, and distillation to smaller models; open-weights release included.

**_DeepSeek-V3 Technical Report_** - DeepSeek-AI - Describes DeepSeek-V3, a 671B MoE model trained at
low cost using FP8 mixed precision, auxiliary-loss-free load balancing, and multi-token prediction pretraining
objectives.

**_Claude’s Character_** - Anthropic - Anthropic’s model card and character overview explaining the values,
persona, and constitutional principles embedded in the Claude model family.

**Inference Systems Engineering Blogs**

**_vLLM: Easy, Fast, and Cheap LLM Serving with PagedAttention_** - UC Berkeley / vLLM Blog - Introduc-
tory blog post accompanying the vLLM open-source release, explaining PagedAttention and demonstrating 24 
throughput gains over HuggingFace Transformers baseline serving.

**_Continuous Batching: How to Serve LLMs 23_**  **_Faster Than HuggingFace_** - Anyscale Engineering Blog

- Engineering walkthrough of how iteration-level (continuous) batching works in practice and why it dominates
static batching for variable-length generation workloads.

**_How to Make LLM Inference Faster with Speculative Decoding_** - Hugging Face Blog - Practitioner-focused
explanation of speculative decoding variants (draft-model, Medusa, EAGLE) with HuggingFacetransformers
integration examples.

**Distributed Training & Infrastructure**

**_Megatron-LM: Continued Training and Fine-tuning for GPT and BERT_** - NVIDIA NeMo / Megatron En-
gineering Blog - NVIDIA’s engineering series covering tensor, sequence, and pipeline parallelism recipes for
Megatron-LM, including practical tuning guides for A100/H100 clusters.

**_ZeRO: Memory Optimizations Toward Training Trillion Parameter Models (DeepSpeed blog)_** - Microsoft
DeepSpeed Blog - Accessible introduction to ZeRO stages 1-3 and ZeRO-Infinity, with empirical memory and
throughput numbers for large-model training.

**_Scaling Distributed Machine Learning with the Parameter Server_** - Li, Andersen, Park, Smola, Ahmed,
Josifovski, Long, Shekita, Su - Classic systems paper introducing the parameter-server architecture for dis-
tributed gradient aggregation; foundational reading before data parallelism and ZeRO.

**_How We Trained Llama 2 at Scale_** - Meta AI Engineering Blog - Meta’s post-mortem of Llama 2 training
infrastructure: FSDP, custom CUDA kernels, fault tolerance, and lessons from training 70B models on clusters
of thousands of GPUs.

**Quantization & Eﬀiciency Engineering**

**_Making LLMs Even More Accessible with bitsandbytes, 4-bit Quantization and QLoRA_** - Hugging Face
Blog - Walkthrough of the QLoRA recipe integrated into the PEFT library, demonstrating fine-tuning of 65B
models on a single 48 GB GPU with NF4 quantisation.

**_Quantization Fundamentals with Hugging Face_** - Hugging Face Blog - Survey of quantisation approaches
(GPTQ, AWQ, SmoothQuant, bitsandbytes) as implemented in the Hugging Face ecosystem, comparing quality
and throughput tradeoffs.

**Data Curation & Pre-Training**

**_What’s in My Big Data?_** - Allen Institute for AI (AI2) Blog - Engineering post accompanying the Dolma
corpus release, detailing data sourcing decisions, quality filtering heuristics, and the open-sourcedolmatoolkit.

**_DataComp-LM: In Search of the Next Generation of Training Sets for Language Models_** - Li, Fang, Smyr-
nis, Ivgi, Jordan, Gadre, Bansal, Guha, Keh, Arora, et al. - Introduces DCLM: a large-scale competition and
dataset for studying data curation strategies, with controlled experiments comparing filtering pipelines for LLM
pre-training.

**Alignment, Safety, and Interpretability**

**_Reward Modeling for Mitigating Sycophancy in RLHF_** - Anthropic Research Blog - Discusses failure modes
of reward models trained on human preferences, specifically sycophancy, and approaches for building more ro-
bust reward signals.

**_Toy Models of Superposition_** - Anthropic Interpretability Team - Mechanistic interpretability study show-
ing that neural networks can represent more features than neurons by using superposition, with implications for
understanding polysemanticity at scale.

**_Scaling Monosemanticity: Extracting Interpretable Features from Claude 3 Sonnet_** - Anthropic Interpretabil-
ity Team - Applies sparse autoencoders to decompose Claude 3 Sonnet residual-stream activations into millions
of monosemantic features, demonstrating that large-scale interpretability is tractable.

**_OpenAI’s Approach to AI Safety_** - OpenAI - Overview of OpenAI’s safety research agenda including RLHF,
red-teaming, interpretability, and preparedness framework for frontier models.

**Evaluation & Benchmarking**

**_Chatbot Arena: An Open Platform for Evaluating LLMs by Human Preference_** - LMSYS / Hugging Face

- Ongoing open leaderboard using blind pairwise human votes to rank LLMs via Elo ratings; the de-facto com-
munity standard for chat-quality comparisons.

**_Open LLM Leaderboard_** - Hugging Face - Automated leaderboard evaluating open-weight models on a
standardised suite (MMLU, HellaSwag, ARC, TruthfulQA, WinoGrande, GSM8K) enabling reproducible open-
model comparisons.

**Recommended Reading Order**

1. **Pick one frontier model report and read it cover to cover.** The Llama 3 report is the most pedagogically
    structured; it covers pre-training data, SFT, RLHF, safety, and infrastructure in one document and maps
    directly onto Parts II-XI of this book.
2. **Systems blogs next.** The vLLM PagedAttention launch post and the Anyscale continuous-batching walk-
    through are short and concrete; read them alongsidechapter 15andchapter 18.
3. **Alignment and interpretability.** Toy Models of Superposition and Scaling Monosemanticity are longer
    reads best saved after finishingchapter 26-chapter 28; they provide the “why” behind reward-model failure
    modes.
4. **Quantisation engineering.** The Hugging Face QLoRA and quantisation-survey blog posts are the fastest
    path from theory to code; pair them withchapter 19.
